name: 48434-cpuoffloadreplay-20b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process engine, one node.
architecture: GptOssForCausalLM, 24 layers alternating sliding (window 128) and full attention, 12 of each; 64 query heads, 8 key/value heads, head_dim 64, hidden 2880, mxfp4 MoE weights with bf16 attention. Shapes are in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=32, warmup 15%, cooldown 10%. 32 is the declared operating point.
workload: prefix replay against the CPU offload tier. 96 unique 4096-token prefixes, each followed by 32 prompt tokens, generating 64 tokens, bounded at 3840 requests -- 40 passes over the set, of which the first seeds the tier and the remaining 39 replay it. Greedy sampling (temperature 0) and a static seed of 48434.
purpose: A 20-billion-parameter assistant answering repeat questions on shared 4,000-token documents, 32 concurrent streams, single GPU.
launch:
# Engine arguments.

model: openai/gpt-oss-20b

# Load-bearing: with the GPU prefix cache off a repeated prompt is not served out of
# GPU-resident blocks, so its prefix is fetched back from the host tier.
enable-prefix-caching: false

# The host-memory KV tier: `CPUOffloadingSpec`, the default single tier (pinned host memory
# in-process, no secondary tier and no router), sized at 32 GiB.
# KEEP ON ONE LINE: the engine's config reader is line-based and skips indented lines, so
# writing this as a nested mapping drops the key silently and the engine starts with no tier
# at all, rc=0.
kv-transfer-config: {"kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"cpu_bytes_to_use": 34359738368}}

tensor-parallel-size: 1

# Worst case on the wire is a 4096-token prefix + 32 prompt tokens + 64 output tokens = 4192.
max-model-len: 8192
